clue.text: Rural, but mostly having officer in charge

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word but is kept, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: A country scene described as overseen by an officer in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter from 'but'. 'having' is only a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic is a literary word for pastoral, describing countryside life.

clue.text: It's an advantage around Tyneside to enjoy good health

indicators.note: around means the phrase for being healthy goes round the region

parts.note: to be fit is to enjoy good health
Tyneside, around Newcastle, lies in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: Living in the north-east is said to help one stay healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' here also suggests 'in the region of', which helps the surface. Tyneside, the Newcastle area, is in the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a gain or helpful result, something in one's favour.

clue.text: Agreeing to deceive fellow about game

parts.note: to con someone is to trick them

indicators.note: about means the word for fellow is placed round the game

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Swindling a chap over a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the game inside the fellow. 'game' stands for rugby union, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Congruent means in agreement or harmony, consistent with something.

clue.text: Strip of wood concealing key for lock

indicators.note: concealing means the strip of wood hides the key inside it

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: A piece of timber hiding a key to a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like a door key, but it is the musical key C.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a simple bar fastening for a door or gate.

clue.text: Commander of, organised unit once, right?

indicators.note: organised means the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A leader asking whether a unit was once properly arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is left open: a centurion commanded a century, a hundred men, in the Roman army. 'organised' rearranges UNIT ONCE plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A centurion led a company of about a hundred Roman soldiers.

clue.text: Make impassioned speech rejecting man with title

indicators.note: rejecting suggests throwing back, so the short name for a man is turned round

parts.note: Ed is a common short man's name
a title is a right or entitlement to something, a claim

explanation.surface: Someone orates passionately while spurning a titled gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns the man round. A title is a legal right to property, which is why it works as a word for a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to deliver a speech in a loud, rhetorical, emotional manner.

clue.text: Measure bolero, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a measure is an old word for a stately ...
the bolero is a Spanish ... in triple time

explanation.definitionFit: A measure was a formal dance, and the bolero is an example of one.

clue.text: Part of Ulster lacking yen to initiate launch

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the currency letter is removed

parts.note: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: An Irish county short of Japanese money to start a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland; take out Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A countdown is the backward counting of seconds before a rocket lift-off.

clue.text: Joint to chafe, starting right away

indicators.note: starting points to the first letter of the word for chafe
away means the letter for right is taken off

parts.note: to rankle is to irritate or chafe

explanation.surface: A joint rubbing sore once you begin walking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting right away' drops the first letter, R, from RANKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint between the foot and the leg.

clue.text: Theatrical performance from China, gripping in English

indicators.note: gripping means the word for friend holds the next piece inside

parts.note: china is cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: A show from China, with English holding the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C on China is there to mislead: china is cockney rhyming slang (china plate). 'gripping' puts IN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance at a theatre or cinema.

clue.text: The composition of a baseball team, for example

definitions.text: The composition of a baseball team, for example

parts.words: The composition of a baseball team, for example
parts.note: a baseball side fields nine players, and a musical piece written for nine performers bears the same name, so 'composition' does double duty

explanation.surface: A question about how many make up a baseball side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks like make-up of the team, but it also means a piece of music, one scored for nine players.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine or a musical work for nine instruments, and a baseball side has nine players.

clue.text: Catch a new food in this island

indicators.note: in tells us the other pieces sit inside the word for catch

parts.note: to catch fish is to net them
tuck is British schoolboy slang for food, especially sweets and snacks

explanation.surface: An invitation to land a fresh meal on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the three pieces inside the word for catch. Tuck is British school slang for snacks; the island lies off Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantucket is an island off Cape Cod in Massachusetts, once a whaling centre.

clue.text: Female member with business in Jones's dwelling

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
a house is a firm, as in a publishing house

explanation.surface: A woman joins a firm and moves into Mr Jones's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Jones is the farmer in Orwell's Animal Farm, so his home is a farmhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmer Jones owns Manor Farm in Orwell's novel, so the house he lives in is a farm residence.

clue.text: Association that's secured by money

indicators.note: secured by means held fast inside the word for money

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A partnership that is guaranteed by cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured by' puts the Latin abbreviation (id est) inside old British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a link or connection, such as a product linked to a film.

clue.text: Fool exporting article from European port

indicators.note: exporting means sending out, so the article is removed from the port

parts.note: Antwerp is a major port in Belgium
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dimwit sending goods abroad from a continental harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exporting' looks like trade, but it sends AN out of ANTWERP.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or annoying person, a nitwit.

clue.text: Articulate as he, say, and extremely capable

parts.note: he is an example of a pronoun

indicators.note: extremely means the outer letters at each extreme of the word are used

explanation.surface: Speaking as he would, and very competently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' is the verb, not the adjective. 'extremely' takes C and E from 'capable'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to articulate a word, saying its sounds clearly.

clue.text: Safe from harm within plant, you might say

indicators.note: you might say signals that the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: within is in and the plant is a violet, giving the phrase in violet

explanation.surface: A creature sheltering safely among the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within plant' means IN VIOLET, which said aloud sounds like INVIOLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inviolate means untouched or unbroken, kept free from injury or violation.

clue.text: Fanciful verse is written on trains crossing island

indicators.note: crossing means the island is placed across the gap between the pieces

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs trains
Iona is an island in the Scottish Hebrides

explanation.surface: Imaginative poetry scribbled on trains travelling over an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts the Hebridean island between the two pieces either side of it; 'written on' simply sets the verse and 'is' in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Visionary describes ideas that are imaginative or idealistic rather than practical.

clue.text: Fictional work in' which a knight can love madly

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
a tin is a can

indicators.note: madly indicates the following letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A romance in which a knight is capable of reckless passion.
explanation.walkthrough: N (knight in chess) and TIN (can) join A and LOVE, and 'madly' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: An antinovel is a work of fiction that deliberately rejects conventional novel form.

clue.text: Extrovert son's expenditure

parts.note: an extrovert person is sociable and outgoing
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: How much a lively young man spends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extrovert' looks like a noun to define, but it is an adjective supplying the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings is the British word for money that is spent, the opposite of income.

clue.text: Something, from the horse's mouth spoken about and going all round the town

indicators.note: about means the word for spoken goes around the bit

parts.note: oral means spoken
a bit is the metal mouthpiece of a horse's bridle

explanation.surface: Information straight from a reliable source about a ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the horse's mouth' suggests inside information, but it is the BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital road is a ring road circling a city.

clue.text: In Near East, it's a preservative for foods

indicators.note: In means the word it is placed inside the abbreviations for near and east

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A substance from the Middle East used to keep food from spoiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near East' looks like the Levant, but near and east are abbreviated separately, and 'In' puts IT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, or saltpetre, has long been used to cure and preserve meats.

clue.text: For example, catching archdeacon at home late in the day

indicators.note: catching means the abbreviation for example holds the others inside

parts.note: e.g. is short for exempli gratia, for example
Ven, Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
in means at home

explanation.surface: Finding the archdeacon at home after dark, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening is the part of the day towards its end, before night.

clue.text: Head off, initially, for party

parts.note: bean is slang for the head

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word off is taken

explanation.surface: Leave the head of the table, first of all, for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAN is slang for the head, and 'initially' takes O from 'off'. A beano is British slang for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British informal slang for a celebration or jolly outing.

clue.text: Paid worker wearing a new pinafore

indicators.note: wearing means the worker has the other letters around them like clothing

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is paid for their work

explanation.surface: A professional putting on a new pinafore.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO (professional) goes inside A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a protective garment like a pinafore, tied over clothes.

clue.text: Steering clear of an opinion about OT book

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving A

indicators.note: about means the word for opinion goes round the book

parts.note: a voice is an expressed opinion, as in having a voice
Dan is an abbreviation for Daniel, a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone dodging a view held about a book of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the opinion round the book. Daniel is a book of the Old Testament, which is what 'OT' means.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoidance is the act of keeping away from something, evading it.

clue.text: Blue, no longer green?

definitions.meaning: blue describes risque or explicit material, as in blue films
green means inexperienced or young, so no longer green is grown-up

explanation.definitionFit: Explicit content is labelled for grown-ups, and a person no longer inexperienced has matured.

clue.text: Live' with wife in depressed area

indicators.note: in means the wife goes inside the hollow

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded hollow

explanation.surface: Settling down with one's wife in a gloomy district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressed area' sounds bleak, but it is a DELL, a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside or live somewhere.

clue.text: From tropical source, perhaps, a natural predator

indicators.note: source means origin, so the first letter of tropical is taken
perhaps signals that the following words could be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A creature from the tropics, maybe a natural hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source' takes T from 'tropical'; 'perhaps' turns A NATURAL into ARANTULA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider that hunts its prey.

clue.text: Tenniel's characters otherwise so unlike the Queen of Hearts?

definitions.text: so unlike the Queen of Hearts?

indicators.note: otherwise signals the letters of the name are put in another order

parts.note: John Tenniel illustrated Alice in Wonderland; his name supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A remark on the illustrator of Alice and the harsh Queen of Hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' means letters: the letters of TENNIEL, 'otherwise' arranged. The Queen of Hearts, drawn by Tenniel, shouts 'Off with her head!'
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen of Hearts is merciless, so someone unlike her is forgiving and mild.

clue.text: Seasonal fare you'll reportedly put in book

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is said rather than spelt

parts.note: you'll said aloud sounds like the old word for Christmas
a log is a book recording events, like a ship's log

explanation.surface: Christmas food you'll enter in a record book, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: YULE is an old name for Christmas; a yule log is a chocolate log cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A yule log is a log-shaped chocolate cake eaten at Christmas.
